planting.note: Set divisions or container plants out in spring once frost danger passes, into moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: This species forms a low mound of glossy, rounded evergreen leaves and is grown mainly for its unusually late flowering season, sending up yellow daisy-like flower clusters in late fall into winter when most other shade perennials have already finished. Give it rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, sheltered from drying wind and hard freezes. It is somewhat less cold-tolerant than common Farfugium japonicum selections, so gardeners outside the warmer end of its range should treat it as a container specimen that can be moved under cover in winter. It has also served as a parent species in hybrid leopard plant breeding, valued for extending the bloom season of its offspring into the cooler months.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring or early fall into consistently moist, humus-rich woodland soil in partial to full shade.

directions: This Chinese woodland species produces broad, rounded, coarsely toothed leaves held on long petioles, with a texture and clump habit reminiscent of the more familiar Ligularia dentata but generally more compact. Slender upright stems carry small yellow daisy flowers above the foliage in summer, though the plant is grown primarily for its bold leaf form rather than for showy bloom. It wants steady moisture and part to full shade, since its thin leaves scorch and wilt quickly in dry soil or strong sun. Give it a sheltered woodland setting with a winter mulch at the colder end of its hardiness range, and divide congested clumps in spring to keep them vigorous.
